1. Indigenous Microorganism (IMO) Technology:
   - Cultivate and use IMOs to improve soil health and resilience.
   - Follow the IMO-4 preparation process:
     a. Collect IMO-3 (10 kg)
     b. Mix with field soil (5 kg) and red fine soil or anthill/termite mound soil (5 kg)
     c. Create a heap no more than 20 cm high and cover for two days
     d. Control moisture with Natural Farming inputs like FPJ, FFJ, FAA, and LAB

2. Natural Farming Fertilizer Strategies:
   - Adopt a "feed the soil, not the plant" approach
   - Use fermented plant juices (FPJ) and fruit juices (FFJ) as natural fertilizers
   - Implement fish amino acids (FAA) for additional nutrients
   - Utilize lactic acid bacteria (LAB) to improve nutrient availability

3. Soil Health Focus:
   - Regularly apply IMO-4 to your fields to enhance microbial diversity
   - Maintain soil moisture at 65-70% for optimal microbial activity
   - Use diverse local materials to culture microorganisms, including those from sunny and shaded areas

4. Continuous IMO Application:
   - Collect and prepare IMOs every year for continued soil improvement
   - Adjust moisture content to 65-70% before application by adding natural farming input liquids

These strategies will help improve your soil's ability to withstand climate stresses, enhance nutrient cycling, and promote overall plant health.
